newsitem.title: USA: USX reports threefold jump in second-quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: USX reports threefold jump in second-quarter profits.

text.p: USX-U.S. Steel Group reported a threefold increase in second-quarter profits Wednesday, crediting a continued strong market and good operating and shipment performance.
The Pittsburgh-based steelmaker posted net quarterly income of $97 million, or $1.23 per share, compared with $32 million, or 32 cents a share, in last year's second quarter.
The results beat the consensus analyst forecast of $1.16 per share, according to market research firm First Call.
USX-U.S. Steel generated revenues of $1.7 billion, a 6 percent rise from $1.6 billion a year ago.
The results included one-time charges with an after-tax impact of $13 million, or 15 cents a share, as well as a credit for an exchange of preferred stock of $10 million, or 12 cents a share.
Excluding those charges and 1996 charges, net income was $110 million, or $1.26 a share, vs. $34 million, or 35 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
For the first half, USX-U.S. Steel reported net income of $184 million, or $2.19 a share, compared with $78 million, or 80 cents a share, last year.

"The company's strong financial performance reflected ongoing attention to customer needs, operating efficiencies and cost reductions throughout our facilities," USX Chairman Thomas Usher said in a statement.
Usher expressed optimism about the rest of the year.
"We're seeing a continued healthy order book for sheet (metal) products and improvements in tubular (metal) products," Usher said.
"With current market conditions and anticipated strong operating performance throughout U.S. Steel's facilities, we should be well-positioned to extend these strong first-half results," he said.
USX-U.S. Steel's stock rose 62.5 cents to $35.375 in consolidated midday New York Stock Exchange trading.
